issues.description: Class Bitmap24: the member functions 'save(const std::string&)' and 'set(int,int,char,char,char)' are declared in the template header as private but are called from the example program (main.cpp). The template header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) puts these declarations in the private section (lines 46-57), while the solution header declares the same methods as public (solution_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp, lines 47-57). Because main.cpp (template) invokes bitmap.set(...) (example_program/src/main.cpp, line 44) and bitmap.save(...) (example_program/src/main.cpp, line 228), the private visibility in the template header will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the intended public API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make Bitmap24::save(const std::string&) and Bitmap24::set(int,int,char,char,char) public in the template header to match their usage in main.cpp and the solution. Concretely, move their declarations above the 'private:' marker (or remove the 'private:' label so those declarations are in the public section), e.g. place the 'void save(const std::string &i_filename);' and 'void set(int i_y, int i_x, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b);' declarations in the public area of example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp. This preserves the intended API and allows the example program to compile for students.
